verdict.rationale: Elicit's own docs show users can delete papers from their Library. Deleted papers go to a 30-day recoverable window and are then permanently deleted, which is a real but narrow deletion and retention control. Nothing in the evidence covers configurable retention periods, deleting sessions, chats or uploaded data more broadly, account-level deletion, or a data-retention policy. Missing for 10: configurable retention settings, deletion controls beyond Library papers (sessions, reports, account), a documented retention/data-handling policy, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: They will stay there for 30 days before being permanently deleted, and are recoverable at any point in that window.
